entries.en: Big place.
That your professional opinion, sir?
This makes Jump Zero look like a porta-john. And it's the largest deep space station the Alliance has.
Jump Zero was big. But this is a whole 'nother scale. Look at the ward arms. How do they keep all that mass from flying apart?
Aye, aye, Commander.
Aye, aye, Commander.
There is definitely a gap between their presentation and what's here. Tracking arrivals must be a nightmare.
Commander, do you have a minute?
Sorry, Commander. There's writing on the wall here, but someone isn't reading it.
It's funny. We finally get out here, and the final frontier was already settled.
Do you have some time to talk now, Commander?
You had to make some tough calls to get us this far. And it looks like there's going to be more.
Commander?
Is that an order, Commander?
Commander.
I'd like that.
I don't see how we could have done things any better. At least not without getting to Eden Prime sooner.
Input? Hell. I don't know.
I'm glad there aren't many aliens like the Thorian. I don't think my stomach could take it.
Killing Saren's-- What was Benezia, anyway? Second-in-command? Advisor? Anyway, it should set him back a bit.
Is this an official evaluation, Commander? Or off the record?
Well, they know about the stonewalling you've had from the Council.
I think they're doing all right.
This isn't a station; it's a city.
Why not? We've got oceans, beautiful women, this emotion called love. According to the old vids, we have everything they want.
All right, secure the chatter. We're all FNGs here, but we don't need to make it obvious.
How can they keep tabs on all of this? The Presidium may as well be on another planet.
Make it quick, Lieutenant. I have a lot on my mind.
We'll get things done. I'd rather operate independently than have the brass on our backs anyway.
The Council doesn't want to believe anything's wrong. I'd call it human nature, but...
Let's hear it, Lieutenant. I'm always open to my officers.
Don't you think we're a little past titles?
Shut up and get over here.
I'm not looking for a pet, Kaidan. I'd have gone elsewhere for that.
We'll talk another time, Lieutenant.
We'll talk later, Kaidan.
What's your opinion on the last mission?
The scope is amazing.
No wonder they need us.
What's not to like?
That's enough, you two.
I don't.
Don't worry about it.
I hear you.
I'm listening.
Still calling me "Commander?"
Damn right.
No, a request.
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
Tactical appraisal?
Commander? Are you all right?
I'm sure there's a way to appeal. We're under Alliance authority, after all. Not the Council.
They can't do this. Not after everything we've been through. We're not going to take this, are we?
There has to be a way to appeal. The Alliance isn't under their control yet.
So that's it? We just walk away? We let them win and damn us all?
If I can be of any help, let me know.
You know you can count on me or any of the crew, Commander.
Cut me a little slack, Shepard. It's not like you're easy to read.
Yeah. I always leave a way out. You know that.
I'm here for you. But we're in a rough spot, and the last thing I want to do is muddy things.
Like it's all that clear to start with. Are we the pride of the fleet or not? Are we valued agents or just peons?
It's that easy, huh? Okay, then.
Everything will be fine, Shepard. You'll figure it out.
I could get used to it. I guess we have some downtime to figure out what we are, huh?
Oh, so it's back to business after playing me. You're something else, you know?
We're a little past a lot of things.
What happens if this doesn't work out, Shepard? We mutinied. Stole a prototype warship. If they wanted to get technical, they could throw in kidnapping.
And those damned aliens sure love to get technical, don't they?
Preaching to the choir, Shepard. They're walking into the Reapers' claws.
It'll really hit the fan when we get to Ilos.
If things don't go well, I want you to know-- Well, I've enjoyed serving under you.
Battlefield flirting is one thing, Shepard. There are regs against fraternization.
Well, I suppose breach of protocol will be pretty far down the list of charges at our courts-martial.
You know what? You're right. About everything. I think about losing you and I can't stand it.
The galaxy will just keep going. Everything, even the Reapers, will come around again. But you and I, we are important right now.
Shepard, you make me feel... human.
Careful, Shepard. I might think you are abusing your authority. A serious breach of protocol.
I'm glad you didn't.
This can't change anything, Shepard. This is a good crew. The finest I've served with. I don't want to mess it up.
You're right, of course. This is too important to risk messing up the team.
I swear, though, if anything happens to you....
Take care, Shepard. If you keep me waiting much longer, it damn well better be the end of the galaxy.
I don't know... I mean, the regs against fraternization seem kind of petty now. Taking a stolen ship to face a giant extragalactic war machine...
Seems like the Reapers really know how to play on fears.
We're a hell of an example of humanity's best and brightest, huh?
I don't wanna speak out of turn. I mean, I hope we're close enough after everything we've said already.
Official channels are closed. They were quite clear about that.
The ambassador was no help. We got hung out to dry. Again.
I pushed as hard as I could. They wouldn't listen.
We'll think of something. I just need to figure things out.
We're out of the game for now. I need you to be there while I figure things out.
I'm looking for a little personal support here. Knock off the "good soldier" crap.
Come on, Kaidan. I can get a salute from anyone on this ship. Sometimes I need a shoulder.
I'm sick of it, too. Maybe we need to take a little initiative.
Can't just pull out a good old-fashioned "It'll be all right", can you?
That wasn't so hard, now was it?
If you get me to melt now, when will I figure out how to save the galaxy?
The Council showed a repeated failure to "get it." They were going to bring humanity down with them.
Kaidan, you stopped being a subordinate a long time ago. Don't you think it's time to act like it?
Bunk here tonight, Kaidan. With me.
Hold that thought. There'll be time for us when this is over. I promise.
You're still hesitating? After all we've been through together? What are you afraid of?
Udina is blind to the big picture. It was time to act. If the greatest casualty is my career, we'll be damn lucky.
I don't know about the "example" part. But as far as saving the galaxy, how good are first-timers supposed to be?
I'm just here to get the job done. Let someone else be on the poster.
For now. The Alliance has to catch me before they can strip my rank. What do you need?
I tried. No luck.
Maybe they are.
Don't you think I tried?
Of course not. Just for now.
I need you to stay strong.
God, you're dense.
You could be less officious.
Depends who you ask.
There you go again.
That's better.
Business before pleasure.
What is it?
We're right, they're wrong.
It was time to take control.
We're more than that.
That's all?
Stay with me.
This isn't the time.
We do all right.
I never claimed to be.
There must be millions here. It can't be possible to track everyone coming and going.
They probably just want to keep everything running. It has to be hard keeping all these cultures working together.
I doubt it's personal. It's got to be a balancing act, like every other government.
Or maybe they just don't like humans.
If you expect to get me in a tinfoil miniskirt and thigh-high boots, I want dinner first.
Sir.
That'll be enough, Chief.
Damn straight you can't.
Ready to move out, sir.
Yes, sir. Sorry, sir.
When you put it that way, there's no reason they wouldn't like you.
I mean, us. Humans. Ma'am.
You don't take much shore leave, do you, L-T?
Um, aye, aye, ma'am.
I'll walk drag, ma'am.
Aye, aye, ma'am!
Heh. Oh Lord.
Off the record, I think there's something wrong here.
This Saren is trying to breed an army of krogan. But we can't get backup from the Council?
This Saren is trading people to aliens for some kind of lost knowledge. But we can't get backup from the Council?
This Saren is looking for records on some kind of galactic extinction. But we can't get backup from the Council?
This Saren is looking for a lost mass relay to who-knows-where. But we can't get backup from the Council?
Yeah, I read a lot of those books when I was a kid. Where the hero goes to space to prove himself worthy of a woman he loves. Or, you know. For justice.
Maybe I was a romantic in the beginning. But I thought about it after Brain Camp-- ah, sorry, "Biotic Acclimation and Temperance training."
I'm not looking for "the dream." I just want to do some good. See what's out here.
"Biotic Acclimation and Temperance" didn't last past the airlock. To the kids they hauled in, it was "Brain Camp."
Sorry, "hauled in" is unkind. We were "encouraged to commit to an evaluation of our abilities, so an understanding of biotics could be compiled."
There are worse results of "accidental" exposure to element zero in the womb. Beats the brain tumors some kids grew up with.
Out of a hundred? Maybe sixty have no effect. Thirty suffer "adverse effects." Little things like brain cancer.
The other ten show enough ability to augment with implants. Not always permanent, though. Not like the cancer.
Next thing you know, you're out on Jump Zero. How's a kid supposed to deal with that? A station at the edge of human space?
It's where they did all the "goose chase" FTL research. Before we caught on to using mass effect fields.
It was a sterile research platform when I was there.
The grand gateway to humanity looks a lot better in the vids.
Anyway. This was supposed to be a casual debrief, not a bull session about stuff that happened years ago.
Well, you're welcome. Ma'am.
You make a habit of getting this personal with everyone?
I'll, uh-- I'll need some time to process that, Commander.
But yeah, I'd like that.
Bad habit, ma'am. I do tend to run off at the mouth. I will work on it for my next review.
My mother was downwind of a transport crash. It was before there were human biotics. A little after the discovery of the Martian ruins.
It only gets iffy around '63 when Conatix was running out of first-gen subjects. Until then, they'd relied on accidentals.
None. I'm not questioning the mission. I'm just concerned.
Sorry to have wasted your time, ma'am. It won't happen again.
Yes, ma'am. Sorry to have wasted your time.
I'm right about the mission, though. I know it.
I've been thinking about the Feros mission. How the colony ended up failing.
I've been thinking about the Noveria mission. About what we did to the rachni.
We've played it pretty close to the book so far. But we're a long way from backup. We've got some tough calls to make.
I'm just saying... try to leave yourself a way out. I've seen what cutting corners can do to someone. And I'd hate to have that happen to you, Shepard.
Commander.
Sorry, ma'am. Maybe I got a bad signal. I mean if you're a-- Maybe there's someone else you'd rather confide in. Ma'am.
There's my answer, then. I'm sorry to have bothered you, Commander. I got some mixed signals.
With your permission, I should return to my duties.
I think she's older than both of us put together. But uh, yeah.
She's a very interesting lady. Not to my, uh, tastes. But I never claimed to be big on alien culture.
It's just that-- We don't have much downtime these days. And I like being around you. But I-- I don't want to take up your personal time.
I'm not questioning any decision you've made, Shepard. Let me be clear about that.
It's just my experience that once someone lets something slide, it tends to pick up speed. You get my meaning?
Oh, I'm sure it's just the humidity.
Y--Yes, Commander. Just had some static on my comm. Got some signals wrong. It won't happen again.
I wasn't speaking to you as my commanding officer, ma'am. I don't want to send any bad signals. Just working on what I've picked up.
I, um... I-- I don't want to step on anyone else's toes. Especially if you're a-- Uh, if I have misread your interests.
Maybe that's not my place. I don't want to send any bad signals, Commander. Just, uh, working on what I've picked up.
You tell me if I'm going too far.
No, Commander. Just concerned about the reception of the brass. If things go sour.
I apologize for bringing it up. I know we're getting the job done.
Aye, aye, Commander.
Yes, ma'am. Just had some static on my comm. Got some signals wrong. Won't happen again.
Closed. And we're supposed to accept that?
So, where do you think the best view will be when the Reapers roll through? If we have to sit it out, may as well get a good seat.
And now he expects us to walk away?
I hope I'm not out of line saying that.
You have something up your sleeve, Shepard?
I'm sorry, Shepard. I thought you'd like to talk about it.
I'll take a step back.
Fair enough. We'll put this... "fun" on hold.
I'll make sure the crew stands by for orders. If you've got anything up your sleeve, they'll be ready.
Commander.
Fair enough.
Yeah, I doubt the Reapers listen to our propaganda anyway.
I've wasted enough of your time for now, Commander. We'll have time for personal debriefings later.
We're all in for the duration. You can count on everyone to do their duty.
The Council represents more races than I thought. No wonder they're careful with newcomers.
No wonder the Council treats us like outsiders. We'd be just another drop in a bucket they already can't carry.
At ease, Lieutenant. I can't see her in a skirt, anyway.
That would be inappropriate fraternization, Chief.
All right, laugh it up, Chief. I appreciate the thought, Alenko, but we're on duty here.
I'll let it slide, Lieutenant, but try to control yourself.
What's on your mind, Lieutenant?
Well, well, you're a romantic. Did you sign on for "the dream," Alenko? Secure man's future in space?
I didn't go through BAaT training for my biotics. Tell me about it.
Seems like you beat the odds. How many didn't make it?
"Jump Zero" is Gagarin Station, right? What's it like?
Jump Zero's a long way from home. What was it like?
I wanted to get to know you a little better, that's all. Thanks for the talk, Kaidan.
I didn't say I did this for the whole crew. We should talk again.
No. No, I don't. We'll talk again later.
I pretty much gave up waiting for the good part.
Is there some question about how you were exposed?
I trust you won't have any questions when whatever's coming hits the fan?
I'm sure your letters home are very poignant. Just keep this kind of sentimentality out of the CIC.
We're stuck in this swamp for now, Lieutenant. What's your take?
That's not the appropriate way to address your commanding officer, Lieutenant.
I don't think you should be prying into my affairs.
Someone--? You're referring to our young Prothean expert?
You seem awfully worried about my personal affairs.
Look, you didn't want to talk about Liara, did you? What's your real issue?
Alenko, if you have one failure, it's an inability to speak directly.
Talk to me, Kaidan. You've got a little black raincloud sitting over your head.
I'm tired of this, Lieutenant. I don't care if you have a problem with me chatting up Liara. It's none of your business.
This a personal observation, Kaidan?
We haven't had much off-duty time to talk. You have an issue with how things are going?
I'm listening. Tell me why you feel the need to speak up.
I'm your commanding officer, Alenko. Are you questioning the way I handle things?
Nothing more out of you, Alenko. Dismissed.
Lieutenant, I'm sure you have duties to attend to.
You always this cautious with a sure thing?
I'm glad you're here. It was a frustrating trip before we were grounded.
I'm in no mood to discuss this, Alenko.
I'm sorry. I do appreciate that you're here.
I don't have time to coddle you, Lieutenant. Fun's fun, but my command is on the line.
Just trying to get a sense of where the crew's at. Thoughts?
"Melting pot" is inadequate.
Big club. Why keep humans out?
It's all right.
That would be unprofessional.
It's all right.
Highly inappropriate.
For what?
An old-fashioned view.
Zip it, Lieutenant.
What did they train you for?
Just be ready.
What's the survival rate?
You doubt it was accidental?
Jump Zero
Sounds rough. Go on.
I'm interested.
You're right.
No, just you.
What do you think?
I'm listening.
Personal crap? Not interested.
"Shepard"? How informal.
Are you concerned for me?
I don't need approval.
That's my business, Alenko.
You mean Liara?
Are you jealous?
I think I've heard enough.
I'm here, aren't I?
I don't need this aggravation.
No. Cut to the chase.
Bad experience?
We'll see.
What's your logic?
That's right.
Then keep quiet.
We're not out for long.
Not now, Lieutenant.
Stop being so precious, goof.
You're not. I'm just upset.
Sorry I snapped.
Make it two.
Looking for personal input.
Sorry. I'm not looking to dump any baggage, Shepard.
You know the records about the biotic training out on Jump Zero? They're all classified. Because the Alliance made mistakes.
After first contact, Conatix was set up to track element zero exposures and develop implants for humans.
Once we had an embassy on the Citadel, Conatix could bring in "experts" instead of taking it slow.
Yeah, you could say that. Our instructor was a turian by the name of Commander Vyrnnus.
I told him my dad wasn't in the war. He'd retired to Vancouver. My family had an inland home that matured to new beachfront.
Vyrnnus had it in for me after that. He cut corners, pushed hard. I mean, you either came out a superman or a wreck. And a lot of kids snapped. A few died.
He hurt a girl. Broke her arm.
Like an idiot, I stood up. Didn't know what I was gonna do. Just something.
And Vyrnnus lost it. Beat the crap out of me. Kept shouting how they should have bombed us back to the stone age. That's when the knife came up.
A military-issue talon. Right in my face.
I cut loose. Full biotic kick, right in the teeth. Almost as strong as I can manage now. At seventeen, that's something.
He didn't have time to hate it. I killed him.
Snapped his neck. They probably could've saved him, if they got him to an infirmary quick enough. But they didn't.
Caused a stir when they shipped him home. BAaT training was shut down. Conatix folded a couple years later.
The point of all this--I guess--is that when you cut corners, it's not always obvious who pays for it.
I'm thirty-two, Shepard. You don't serve as long as I have without coming to terms with yourself.
You also learn that if someone is special to you, you help them. Try to keep them from making mistakes.
I got some signals. Maybe some static too, I guess.
If I'm out of line, just say the word.
When someone important to you is up on a ledge, you help them. Keep them from mistakes better made by a kid.
Not as much as it shocked Vyrnnus. It killed him.
Get your knuckles rapped a few times, Lieutenant?
I don't see you snapping very easily. What finally did it?
Sat down by a kid. Vyrnnus must have hated that.
Am I supposed to talk you down now or something? Because I'm not so good at therapy.
Special, huh?
So you think you have leave to talk like we're more than officers?
You're not out of line, Kaidan. But there are regs.
Now isn't the ideal time. But I want to talk about this, Kaidan.
Sorry, Kaidan. This was just a battlefield thing.
So why are you telling me this? Are you saying I'm cutting corners somewhere?
Tapping that deep must have shocked the hell out of you.
Blowhards are easy to brush off. How'd he finally get under your skin?
You had a bad teacher?
What happened?
He finally got to you?
Impressive.
That must have scared you.
This the part where I fix you?
I don't see the connection.
"Special?"
You're assuming a lot.
You're not.
I'm interested, but not now.
You're out of line.
Yeah, that's the official name. Biggest and farthest facility we had for decades. Right on the termination shock, the outer edge of the solar system.
No issue, Shepard. At least, not when you're around.
They didn't know where to start. Hell, it took a couple years to even link biotics and eezo.
Forget trying to get the kids to move stuff. They had trouble just helping them not break their own limbs.
They were afraid of what people back home would think. Asking the turians for help when we'd just fought a war with them.
Yes, but the company didn't go through the Citadel. It would have made Earth look weak. So they discreetly hired some turian mercenaries.
It wasn't best for us. They brought in an ex-military turian named Commander Vyrnnus.
To introduce himself, he liked to say, "I was at the helm of the dreadnought that killed your father."
I get you, Shepard. I don't make a habit of complicating the chain of command.
Just think about what I said.
Sorry. Not sure where I stand. You seem a bit, uh, distracted. By someone.
I don't want to distract you too much. The deeper we get into this mess, the bigger it seems.
I'm just looking for an ear. The debriefing wasn't the right place to say how ridiculous this is.
Seems like every other race in the galaxy is wrapped up in their own problems. They don't want to see what's coming.
We're out here trying to save everyone. We can worry about who's king after the dust settles.
I don't think many of them even want to. A lot of people don't understand that.
Resentment? Against aliens? I'm not-- What makes you think that?
I mean, it's only been 26 years since first contact. That's not a lot of time to understand them.
It was Vyrnnus who made me see how human aliens are. They're not different or special. They're jerks and saints, just like us.
Hell, by the time I got payback, I didn't even want it anymore.
It's funny. I'm not sure which of us got the worst of what happened.
I'm not upset he's dead. Just sorry I killed him. I wasn't prepared for that. I dropped out of sight for a bit.
I didn't. Not at the time. I wasn't upset he was dead, but I was sorry that I'd killed him. So I dropped out of sight for a bit.
They let me go. I guess they wanted it to blow over as much as I did. I came back on my terms, because I wanted to serve.
So yeah, I hated that turian. But he wasn't "a turian" to me. He was Vyrnnus.
Shepard, I outgrew the blame game years ago. If the Alliance is missing its chance, it's because of men like Udina. Not the rest of the galaxy holding it back.
We're not doing the galaxy any favors if we try to force our way into a seat at the grown-up table.
They aren't-- malicious. They're just slow to change. My story doesn't get any better if Vyrnnus is a good guy.
Look, Shepard, you're in command and we'll all follow your lead. But don't ream me out for having an opinion.
I thought we respected each other more than that.
Yeah. I think we are. It's too bad we....
It's just too bad. Commander.
I'm here, Shepard. I'm not going anywhere.
Look, I can't deny they've been reluctant to step up. But with everything we've dumped in their laps...
Sometimes you just get overwhelmed. You don't know what to do, so you don't do anything. I know I was paralyzed after Jump Zero.
That's a low bar for them to be tripping on.
All right. Maybe it would be better if the Alliance had more pull on the Council. In some ways.
You're damned persuasive, Shepard. You should have Ambassador Udina's job.
I hear that. You're something else, you know that?
I don't think we'll be operating without support for much longer. Pretty soon, not even the Council will be able to ignore what's going on.
Glad you'll be here when it's over, Shepard. I'm, uh... I'm looking forward to some shore leave.
You looked like you were about ready to go off on the Council. Much as they deserve it, it's good to take a step back.
What am I saying? When don't you? That's what I-- appreciate about you.
And this is what will never happen again. Us.
Hi, Commander. We're about in the thick of it. I-- I guess I just wanted to say-- Well, it doesn't matter now, I guess.
It's been an honor serving under you, ma'am. I hope we get a chance to shoot the breeze when this is all over.
It's nothing, ma'am. Water under the bridge.
We haven't had a lot of downtime. Soon, maybe.
Anything you need, Commander?
Is there some reason we couldn't learn it on our own?
I'm sure Conatix did what they thought was best.
You seemed decisive then, Lieutenant. Why so hesitant now?
Something to add, Lieutenant, or are you just breaking in your thesaurus?
It's up to the Alliance to take its proper place. Even if we have to kick its ass to convince it to kick theirs.
You sound like you want the aliens dictating to us.
So can I guess this will add to your resentment against aliens?
Don't tell me you and Vyrnnus hugged on graduation day.
I'd think you'd carry a grudge over the crap you took from Vyrnnus.
He's probably got something over you in the regrets department.
You were just a kid. How'd you deal with that mess?
You can't deny the turians are imperialists. And the asari, the salarians -- they're manipulators.
When anyone out here listens to us, the Council starts up with their treaties and heel-dragging. We can only rely on ourselves.
I don't need you kissing the Council's asses too.
I can't believe you'd side with aliens over your own kind. I think we're done here.
I'm sorry. I'm just angry about the whole mess. You've been invaluable. For everything.
The Council isn't Vyrnnus. The Council is you. Gun-shy after past wars. Too worried about what might happen to take action.
They can't make the hard calls. They're too afraid of what might happen. You had more spine as a kid than they're showing now.
They're burying their heads in the sand while Saren rolls over the Terminus Systems. If they won't help themselves, we have a responsibility to save them.
No way you're getting me behind a desk.
And here I was concerned you were damaged goods.
Careful. When this is over, I might pay more attention to what you say.
Galaxy in the balance and you trip talking to me.
You have something you want to say?
I'd have liked to spend more time getting to know my officers, Alenko.
Why couldn't we do it alone?
You do what you have to.
You mean when we flirted.
And?
Smug aliens. We'll show them.
That's your training talking.
Whose side are you on?
What happened with Vyrnnus?
Your experience on Jump Zero.
My money's on Vyrnnus.
It must have freaked you out.
All turians are the same.
I'm glad you think that.
I'm not so sure.
Whose side are you on?
You have it backwards.
True.
I can't respect this.
You're right.
They're afraid.
They're ignoring the problems.
Who'd want it?
Couldn't do worse.
Watch yourself, Romeo.
You tease.
What's this about, Lieutenant?
We haven't had time to talk.
Bunch of guys in suits show up at your door after school. Next thing you know, you're out on Jump Zero.
No one "knows." Doesn't mean they didn't happen. As big as the exposures were, it was hard to track down accidentals.
It was different then. No one knew the potential, so there wasn't a lot of regulation. Anything Conatix did was gold.
I'm not saying they intentionally detonated drives over our outposts. But in retrospect, they were damn quick on the scene.
This is almost over. The Council won't be able to deny what we've found after this.
Ash backed those salarians to the end. And we still can't get any respect.
We all but served evidence of Saren's intent on a platter. And still we don't get any respect.
If they don't want to do anything, they should get the hell out of our way. It could only improve things if the Alliance was in charge.
It's a damn good one. And we're closer than ever, thanks to you.
What? That isn't what you've been pushing?
Didn't you make an argument for pushing the Council out? That the Alliance should demand its due instead of waiting to be accepted?
You're always on top of things.
That's not what I got out of it.
Did I misread you? Geez, what else have I got wrong?
All right. I don't want to get you wrong. I've got a lot tied up in this mission.
I've got a lot tied up in you.
Shepard, I was gearing up to confront the Council. As an officer, you should keep me in the loop.
As a friend, I'd hope I wouldn't have to remind you of that. Maybe-- maybe I got the message wrong.
It sure feels like it. I'm sorry, I need to take a step back and have a look at this.
Maybe I do, Commander.
I should return to my duties anyway. Commander.
We're so close now. When we deliver everything, the Council will have to mobilize around us.
It would be a fitting tribute to Ash if we were able to rally everyone together under the Council.
